newsitem.title: USA: Decision on raising Intertie power flow seen Fri.
newsitem.headline: Decision on raising Intertie power flow seen Fri.

text.p: A study group convened by the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) is expected to decide Friday on a proposal to raise capacity limits on major power lines linking the Pacific Northwest to California.

A spokeswoman for the WSCC said the panel will decide whether or not to endorse a proposal by Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) to immediately raise the limits by 25 percent to 6,500 megawatts (MW).
If the study group endorses the plan, it will be submitted to the WSCC board of trustees which would have 10 days to accept or reject it, she added.
If the panel does not endorse the proposal, lines will remain capped near 65 percent, the level at which they have been limited since two power blackouts hit the West last summer.
BPA said it has put in place a series of measures to enhance system reliability and voltage support.
The federal agency also plans system upgrades which would allow the lines to return to full capacity by April.
